description: Three managers: the Python package (pyproject.toml and uv.lock), the UI (ui/package.json and its lockfile), and the GitHub Actions. uv.lock picks each release CI and the golden tests run, so every bump arrives as a pull request those tests gate. The MCP bundle's pyproject.toml is left out: the release sets its pins. Lock-file refreshes stay off (the shared default): npm cannot hold a refresh to the 14-day wait, and uv can only with exclude-newer = "14 days" in pyproject.toml, which cannot resolve yet: the SDK's >=0.8.1 floor has no release that old until 0.8.1 (uploaded 2026-11-19) ages in after 2026-12-03, and pgkeyset 0.2.0 (2026-11-13) after 2026-11-27. A refresh would move the SDK within its range without dashboard approval, and tests/test_mcpb.py fails it until mcpb/pyproject.toml's constraint moves with it.

packageRules.description: The MCP bundle pins the released package and holds the SDK to the version in uv.lock (tests/test_mcpb.py); the release moves both, never Renovate.

Golden tests hold the wire contracts nimblebrain-server-sdk and pgkeyset produce. pgkeyset is pinned exactly; the SDK is held to a minor range and uv.lock picks its version. A bump of either is a deliberate, reviewed change, never part of a group.
